advances: A conditional attainment for one fixed positive family of arbitrary compact convex fibers. It neither imposes fixed-base shape minimality nor preserves lattice completeness under general projective maps.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The projective law proved in 6b80e85ff6937910 identifies each geometric image measure with the weights $L(p)^{-d}$ on the original fixed fibers and matches closed-halfspace traces. That portion of its proof holds for every positive denominator on any positive compact convex compatible family, prior to any minimality assumption. In particular normalization of $L$ by a common positive scalar does not change depth. The same positive chart preserves convex traces on the base: for $U\subset P$, a nonempty trace is characterized by $P\cap\operatorname{conv}U=U$, and the chart maps convex hulls exactly to the hulls of their images. Thus Helly numbers are preserved. The empty trace is also preserved.

The normalized nonnegative affine arrays form a compact subset of a closed simplex. Each array is a limit of positive affine arrays by mixing with the constant array one. On the positive part, the normalized weights are continuous. For two probability measures on the fixed sampled set, every cap probability differs by at most total variation, and taking the infimum over containing caps then the supremum over marks preserves that bound. The supremum is a maximum: for fixed normal, the closed through-mark cap mass is upper semicontinuous in the mark by the closed threshold inequality and the reverse Fatou inequality for bounded integrands; the infimum over normals is upper semicontinuous on the compact sampled set.

Let a sequence approach a boundary array, whose zero set $F$ is a nonempty proper exposed-face trace. Each term $|K_p|L_j(p)^{-d}$ with $p\in F$ tends to infinity, and the terms outside stay bounded. Thus the fraction of mass carried by $F$ tends to one. Restrict the original fibers to $F$, where compatibility persists, and transform them using the same full projective chart. The result is an actual positive family on $F_{L_j}$ with fewer sites and Helly number $h(F)$ by trace preservation. The assumed smaller-base bound therefore gives restricted normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/h(F)$ for each $j$. Ambient halfspaces restrict to intrinsic halfspaces or whole and empty traces on the retained affine plane, and intrinsic halfspaces extend to ambient ones. A deepest retained mark consequently has full-family depth at least its restricted depth times the mass fraction carried by $F$. Every convex trace on the exposed face is a convex trace on $P$, by taking the convex hull of that trace within the face. The corresponding minimal infeasible families show $h(F)\le h(P)$. These arguments give the lower limit with no requirement on relative rates of the denominators.

A minimizing sequence has a convergent subsequence in the compact closure. The strict initial gap prevents a boundary limit, so interior continuity yields an attained positive array. Composing with any further small positive denominator $a+b\cdot p'$ at image coordinates $p'=p/L_*(p)$ gives the affine denominator $aL_*(p)+b\cdot p$ on the original base, positive there. Hence the resulting image is locally minimal within the stated orbit.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $P\subset\mathbb R^r$ be finite and affinely spanning, and let $(K_p)_{p\in P}$ be a fixed actual compatible family of positive compact convex $d$-fibers. Translate the base so that $0$ lies in the relative interior of its hull. For affine $L>0$ on $P$, let $D(L)$ be maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth of the unweighted projective image $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$. Let $h(P)$ denote the Helly number of convex-set traces on $P$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Suppose that for every finite base $Q$ with fewer sites than $P$, every actual positive compatible $d$-fiber family on $Q$ has maximum normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/h(Q)$. Normalize $\sum_{p\in P}L(p)=|P|$. If a sequence $L_j$ tends to a nonnegative boundary array with zero set $F\subset P$, then
$$
\liminf_j D(L_j)\ \ge\ \gamma_d/h(F)\ \ge\ \gamma_d/h(P).
$$
If $D(1)<\gamma_d/h(P)$, the infimum of $D(L)$ over positive affine denominators is attained at a positive denominator and remains strictly below the target. The minimizing image is locally minimal under further positive affine projective changes.
title: Conditional projective orbit attainment for any fixed positive compatible family
